newsitem.title: UKRAINE: Ukraine president approves 30 pct T-bill tax.
newsitem.headline: Ukraine president approves 30 pct T-bill tax.

text.p: Ukraine's President Leonid Kuchma gave final approval to a new 30 percent tax on business profits which will include taxing earnings from discount Treasury bills purchased at auction, Kuchma's press service said on Thursday.

Ukraine's government and parliament are steadily approving a series of nine tax laws designed to underpin the 1997 budget, expected to be passed by the end of the month and essential for a multi-billion dollar International Monetary Fund (IMF) credit.
"The new law has been signed with a view to passing this year's budget," the press service said.
The tax on T-bills, tax-free since Ukraine starting selling them in early 1995, will take effect from July 1.
Ukraine's T-bill market was expected to cover a significant portion of this year's budget deficit, projected at 5.7 percent of gross domestic product.
The former Soviet republic has been operating without a budget since January 1, the deadline set under Ukrainian law.
